Description:
Bring home an exciting educational experience with this 48-piece rock and mineral collection kit. The set includes an original display box, a blue plastic tray with 48 slots (a few may be missing stones), and a colorful fold-out poster with vivid images and information for each rock and mineral featured in the collection. Included are a variety of polished and raw stones, from classic rose quartz to unique textured specimens and a heart-shaped clear stone. The kit offers a wonderful visual and tactile variety for collectors, students, or those curious about geology. Each item is photographed to display its specific characteristics, while the included guide enhances learning and identification for each stone. The set as shown is in used condition with some stones potentially missing and visible wear to the packaging. Perfect for an educational gift, a hands-on science tool, or a starter set for amateur collectors

description:
Pressed Glass Telegraph Insulator Lot - 2 Pieces
W. Brookfield, CD 145 Beehive Style
Aqua Blue-Green, Antique Circa 1880s-1890s
Pair of authentic antique CD 145 "Beehive" style glass telegraph and telephone insulators manufactured by the W. Brookfield Glass Company of New York. Featuring heavy molded aqua glass construction with a pronounced wire groove, rounded dome crown, and interior threaded petticoat skirt, these classic insulators played a vital role in early American telecommunications and railroad line infrastructure.
Pieces Included:
Brookfield CD 145 Beehive insulator, embossed "W. BROOKFIELD NEW YORK" and "PAT. NOV. 13TH 1883 / FEB. 12TH 1884", aqua glass, approximately 4 inches tall - intact with light base fleabites
Brookfield CD 145 Beehive insulator, matching form with inner petticoat threading, aqua glass, approximately 4 inches tall - intact with minor rim roughness
Condition:
Both insulators are structurally sound with intact crowns, smooth wire tie grooves, and clear internal threading. Base rims display typical light fleabites, minor flaking, and mold seam roughness consistent with authentic vintage field use and age. Glass exhibits characteristic maker inclusions and air bubbles throughout with strong aqua color and gloss.
***Condition Disclaimer***
This is a USED item donated to Goodwill Easter Seals of the Miami Valley.

This collection features a variety of natural mineral and crystal specimens including a druzy quartz geode slice, blue lace agate slice, polished agate slices, and an amethyst cluster section. - Amethyst cluster section featuring purple crystal points surrounding a hollow center

Each specimen shows natural variation in color, size, and crystal formation typical of geological samples.

This lot includes two vintage smoking pipes with distinct styles. Both pipes display wear and patina consistent with their age and show craftsmanship typical of collectible smoking pipes.

description:
Decorative Stone Egg Lot - 7 Pieces
Polished Marble, Onyx, Calcite, and Mineral Specimens
Includes 2 Ornate Metal Display Stands
A distinctive collection of seven carved and polished natural stone eggs featuring varied mineral compositions, banded patterns, and rich colorations. Polished hardstone eggs have long been collected as tactile curios and decorative accents, showcasing the natural geological beauty of stones such as onyx, marble, and quartz. Each piece exhibits smooth contours and an all-around gloss polish.
Items Included:
Banded onyx/calcite egg with cream and tan strata
White and grey veined marble egg on stand
Cobalt blue quartz/mineral egg on stand
Polished red jasper/marble egg
Bright yellow calcite/alabaster egg
Swirled grey and white marble egg
Petite purple lepidolite/fluorite egg
Two ornate gold-tone metal tripod display stands
Condition:
All eggs remain in good condition with smooth, lustrous finishes. Minor natural mineral pits and internal fissures characteristic of authentic stone lapidary specimens. Both metal tripod stands are structurally sound and stable with light age-appropriate patina.

No. 55 Transposition Insulator (CD 205)
Pressed Glass, Aqua Blue, Vintage Early to Mid-20th Century
Vintage Hemingray No. 55 CD 205 aqua glass transposition insulator, historically utilized on rural telephone and power transmission lines to rotate and swap wire positions to minimize electrical crosstalk interference. Manufactured in Muncie, Indiana, this distinctive style of American industrial glass remains a popular favorite among telegraph, utility, and antique glass collectors.
Distinctive transposition profile featuring spiral wire guide channels across the upper dome
Pressed aqua blue glass containing natural manufacturing swirl patterns and authentic seed air bubbles

This natural geological specimen consists of a substantial plate of translucent crystalline selenite (gypsum) anchored to a sandy sedimentary rock matrix. Specimens retaining their natural host rock provide valuable educational and aesthetic display value for mineral collectors.

description:
Set of 3 Vintage Hemingray 42 and Whitall Tatum Glass Insulators
This set includes three vintage glass insulators used for telegraph or power lines. It features two Hemingray-42 insulators, one in aqua blue glass and one in clear glass, both embossed with branding and model numbers. The set also includes one Whitall Tatum Co. insulator in light blue aqua glass with embossed markings. Each insulator has ridged designs and domed tops characteristic of early to mid-20th century utility glassware. These pieces show minor wear consistent with vintage use and are suitable for collectors interested in historical or decorative items.

description:
Hemingray Glass Company Set - 2 Pieces
Hemingray 42 (CD 154)
Aqua, Vintage Mid-Century
This set features two vintage aqua glass insulators produced by the Hemingray Glass Company, identified by the "Hemingray-42" mold mark. The No. 42 model, classified as CD 154 by collectors, was one of the most widely used designs for telephone and telegraph lines across North America during the early-to-mid 20th century. Prized for their deep aqua color and iconic industrial aesthetic, these pieces represent a significant era of American telecommunications history and are staple items for glass insulator collectors.
Pieces Included:
Glass Insulator, Hemingray 42, Aqua, Beaded Base - minor fleabites on drip points
Glass Insulator, Hemingray 42, Aqua, Beaded Base - minor fleabites on drip points

Both insulators are in good vintage condition with characteristic wear expected from outdoor utility use. The glass retains high clarity and its original vibrant aqua hue. As is common with authentic vintage insulators, there are minor fleabites and small chips along the sharp drip points on the beaded base.
